## TidyVerse Assignment

```{r}
#Loading the package, tidyverse
library(tidyverse)

```

## Introduction:

I'd like to look at correlation between:

1\) Different genders and their glucose levels\
2) Different household income and glucose levels\
3) People with glucose vs parents having diabetes or not.

```{r}
#Loading diabetes dataset from Kaggle.com
DiabetesData <- read.csv(
  "https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=1KeT2EImIqQS6IUuRGZfePNNrDMB6F8jh&export=download&confirm=t"
)

```

```{r}
# Group the data by age group and gender
DiabetesData %>% group_by(age_group, gender)%>%

  # Calculate the average random glucose level for each group
  summarise(
    avg_glucose = mean(random_glucose_mg_dl)
  )

#loading graphing library to analyse and visualize the data 
library(ggplot2)

# Group the data by age group and gender, then calculate the
# average random glucose level for each group.
DiabetesData %>%
  group_by(age_group, gender) %>%
  
 # Calculate the average glucose level and remove the grouping
  # from the resulting data frame.
  summarise(
    avg_glucose = mean(random_glucose_mg_dl),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  
  # Create a bar chart with age group on the x-axis,
  # average glucose on the y-axis, and gender represented by fill.
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = avg_glucose, fill = gender)) +
  
  
  # Create side-by-side bars for each gender within each age group.
  geom_col(position = "dodge")





```

```{r}
# Create a new data frame called "db" by selecting the variables
# needed for the analysis from the DiabetesData dataset.
db <- DiabetesData %>% 
  select(annual_income,
         gender,
         age_group,
         weight_kg,
         random_glucose_mg_dl)

# Create a scatter plot to examine the relationship between
# annual income and random glucose levels.
ggplot(db, aes(x = annual_income, y = random_glucose_mg_dl)) +
  
   # Add individual data points to the plot.
  # A low alpha value makes the points more transparent,
  # which helps when many points overlap.
  geom_point(alpha=0.1)+
  
 # Add a linear regression line to show the overall trend
  # between annual income and random glucose level.
  geom_smooth(method="lm")

# There seems to be no / week correletion between annual income and diabetes / glucose levels 



```
